title: The War Precautions Act and the home front
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:18Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:51Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No single bank point teaches the whole brief: the German Australians card covers only internment, the propaganda and censorship card covers only censorship, and the women's card covers only home-front work, so the new point's combined idea of the War Precautions Act's powers and the home front needs its own card.

draft.title: The War Precautions Act and the home front
card: The War Precautions Act 1914 gave the Australian government wide powers in wartime. It was passed soon after the war began.
Under the Act, the government could censor news and letters, control parts of the economy, and intern some people. Internment means holding people in a camp without a normal trial.
Many of those interned were people of German background, even when they had lived in Australia for years. Some had been born in Australia.
The home front means the people and work at home during a war. Women and others raised money, made items such as socks and bandages, and sent supplies to soldiers.
draft.remember: The Act gave the government wide powers at home, while ordinary people raised money and supplies.

a.q: Why was the War Precautions Act important for the home front?
opts: It gave the government wide powers over daily life
It sent women overseas to nurse soldiers
It let voters decide if men must fight overseas
It made Australia join the war on Britain's side
a.why: The Act gave the government powers such as censoring news, controlling the economy and interning people. The vote on fighting overseas was a separate event, and the Act was not what brought Australia into the war.
a.clue: Think about what the government could do to people at home.

b.q: In 1916 a newspaper editor in Adelaide is told not to print a report about a battle. Which power in the War Precautions Act does this show?
b.why: Stopping a report from being printed is censorship of the news. Controlling the economy deals with matters such as goods and prices, and raising money was done by people and groups at home, not a power of the Act.
b.clue: The government is controlling what the public can read.

a.best: It gave the government wide powers over daily life
